name: Sports
description: Keeps each person's followed leagues and teams, private to the owner. A whole league can be followed once, and following it again returns the saved follow. A followed team is tied to the provider's permanent team number. The standings picker remembers the leagues a person chose and the standings view they last opened, under the same saved settings as before. Account export and deletion cover all six Sports tables. The package reads ESPN's public data for the league catalog, each league's team list and club search, and keeps a shared copy so one person's lookup serves everyone. The copy holds only public sports data, never a person's follows or searches. Following a team checks the live team list and is refused, with the same fail-closed messages the old app gave, when ESPN is down. Scoreboard, standings and news reading are built but not yet offered as routes. A person can add news sources of their own, up to ten, each a website with a news feed or a subreddit, and choose which sports and followed teams each one covers, up to twenty choices in all. Adding a source shows a preview first, which names the reason when a site cannot be used, and a source saves only after the person confirms it. Two subreddits that differ only by letter case are one source. The package reads those public sites itself, and keeps unconfirmed previews for ten minutes under the person's own saved settings. A site with no feed can get a recipe that the person's chosen AI model proposes. The recipe is a strict description of one public address and where the headlines sit in it, it may only name sites the person already confirmed, and it is saved only after a real replay finds headlines. Sources are read again on a schedule without a browser or article text, each source shows whether it is healthy, drifted or missing its recipe, and a person can retry a source or rebuild its recipe after confirming a preview. Nine chat tools list, preview, confirm, retry, rebuild and remove sources. Every change asks the person first, showing a card built from the saved source and the stored preview, and removing a source asks before it deletes. When a site shows no headlines until its scripts run, adding or rebuilding a source from the screen can open the page in a sandboxed browser, and the AI model proposes the recipe from what the browser saw. A machine that cannot run the browser safely, or a chat tool, keeps the plain reading. Headline photos, the followed-team chat tools and the screens are not part of this package yet.

settings.label: Sports
settings.description: Followed leagues and the standings choices can be changed through the Sports routes. The Settings page for them is not part of this package yet.

settings.label: News sources
settings.description: Added news sources and the sports each one covers can be managed through the Sports routes. The Settings page for them is not part of this package yet.

features.description: Each person keeps private follows of whole leagues and of single teams. Following a whole league twice returns the first follow, so a league never appears twice. Removing a follow deletes only the person's own row. Following a team, or changing which team a saved follow means, is checked against ESPN's team list for that league, and is refused while ESPN cannot be reached. Chat can also follow or unfollow a league or team after the person approves a card showing exactly what changes, and unfollowing something not followed changes nothing.

errors.description: ESPN's team list is not available right now, so a team cannot be checked or followed.

remediations.description: Follow the whole league for now, then pick the team once ESPN answers again.

features.description: Follows are tied to the provider's permanent team number, so two teams sharing a short name never swap scores. A team saved before that is put on hold and Sports asks once which team was meant; picking one brings it back. The pick is checked against ESPN's team list for that league.

Sports lists every league and tournament it covers, grouped by confederation. A league's clubs load only when that league is opened, and club search looks across every league. Search fetches at most five leagues that are not stored yet, and stops sooner if it has spent about two seconds, and reports that coverage is partial until the rest fill in. A search needs at least two characters. The screens for these are not part of this package yet.

errors.description: The league is not in the catalog, so its clubs are not looked up.

features.description: The standings picker keeps the leagues a person chose and the competition and view they last opened, on any device, until they pick another. A name that is not a known league is refused. The picker itself is not part of this package yet.

The Sports overview lists a person's followed clubs as cards, one card per club even when the club is followed in several competitions, with live or finished game, last five results, next match and league standing. It also lists each followed competition's recent games and standings. Games on ESPN's evening slate land on the right day because days are counted in US Eastern time. With nothing followed it shows a default slate of major leagues. A follow saved without a permanent team id is listed for the person to resolve and never gets a score. Headlines come from ESPN's league and club news, limited to the sports and teams the person's coverage allows. The top stories lead with each league's first story and then stories about followed clubs, up to six, and a story already on a club card is not repeated. The hero shows gameday slides, live games first, from fifteen minutes before a game starts until it ends, and shows the lead story when no followed game is on. The featured story is the heaviest story with art, a summary and a followed club, and its body is read from ESPN's article page as the first three paragraphs in plain text, at most 900 characters, or falls back to the summary when ESPN cannot be read. Stories from custom sources and the less-of-this filter are not part of the overview yet.

errors.description: ESPN did not answer, so the overview carries what is cached and marks itself degraded.

remediations.description: Open the Sports overview again in a few minutes, when ESPN answers.

features.description: A competition's standings load on demand, with each conference and division as its own view. Once a tournament's group stage is complete, the answer also carries the games around today so the screen can show the bracket.

The latest completed result for one club reads from ESPN over the last ninety days, using the person's follows to find the club and every competition they follow it in. A name that matches more than one club asks the person to choose, and a result the source could not provide is reported as unavailable, never guessed.

A person adds a news source of their own by typing a website address or a subreddit. The preview reads the public site and shows the sources it found with sample headlines, or names why it cannot be used. Saving needs the person's confirmation that they may read the site, and a preview expires after ten minutes. A person keeps at most ten added sources and twenty source choices in all, and a source that is already saved, including a subreddit differing only by letter case, is not added twice. Changing which sports and teams a source covers uses the same preview and confirm steps, and is refused if the source changed in between. Removing a source deletes it and its choices. A source icon is looked up on the site and shown only when it is a real image.

errors.description: The site could not be read, was blocked, asked for a login or sign-in, or limited how often it can be read.

The site has no news feed and the AI model could not give a recipe that finds headlines on the sites already confirmed, so it cannot be added. If the site only shows headlines after its scripts run and this machine cannot open the sandboxed browser, it cannot be added either.
The person already has ten added sources or twenty source choices.

remediations.description: Try the site's feed address, or a subreddit such as r/nfl, instead of the home page.

features.description: A website with no news feed gets a recipe from the person's chosen AI model. The model is told which sites are allowed and a reply naming any other site is refused. The recipe is checked against a strict shape, then replayed once through the real fetch, and it is saved only if the replay finds at least one headline. Reading a saved source never opens a browser and never fetches article text. Each source shows a health state. A page that changed shape marks the recipe as drifted, a source without a usable recipe is marked missing, and a person can retry it now or rebuild the recipe from a preview they confirm, which is refused if the source changed in between. A rebuild never changes which site the source belongs to.

errors.description: No AI model is set up or it did not answer, so a recipe could not be proposed.
The saved recipe no longer finds headlines because the page changed.

remediations.description: Rebuild the recipe from the source's preview and confirm it, or retry the source later.

features.description: When the plain page gives the AI model no usable recipe, adding a source or rebuilding a recipe from the screen opens the home page once in a sandboxed browser that has no network of its own. The model then sees the page text and a few links as the browser rendered them, still only as data, and its recipe is checked and replayed exactly as before, through the plain fetch. Only the sites the person already confirmed can be opened. The browser is never used by a refresh, by a scheduled read, or by a chat tool. A machine that cannot run the browser safely, a busy or slow browser, or a page that shows nothing keeps the plain-fetch result, so the preview says the site is unsupported.

errors.description: The sandboxed browser is not set up on this machine, is busy, or took too long, so a script-driven site was read without it.

remediations.description: Try the site's feed address or a subreddit, or try again in a minute.

features.description: Nine chat tools manage added sources. Listing, previewing a new source, previewing new coverage and previewing a recipe rebuild only read. Confirming a source, new coverage or a rebuilt recipe, retrying a source and removing a source each ask the person first. Removing asks before it deletes. The approval card is built from the saved source, the saved follows and the stored preview, never from the model's text, and the approval is tied to that card: if the source, a follow or the preview changed since, the tool refuses and asks again. A confirm uses its preview once and a preview lasts ten minutes. A tool refusal carries the same wording the routes give.

errors.description: The source, a follow or the preview changed after the person approved, so the change was not made.

remediations.description: Ask for the change again so a fresh card can be reviewed.

features.description: ESPN headlines can cover chosen sports and followed teams. With no choice made the default coverage applies, and saving an empty choice turns ESPN headlines off. A followed team the person does not have is refused.

Sports gives the daily briefing a short list of facts for the person's followed teams and leagues in their own time zone, covering games live now, still to play today and finished. A person who follows nothing sees the default leagues. When the scoreboards cannot be read, the briefing says so and shows no facts. A heartbeat tool lists the next followed fixtures from stored scoreboards only and reports whether they are fresh, stale or unknown.

sports.listSources.description: List the active actor’s bounded public sports sources, assignments, health, timestamps, and safe recovery status. Never returns recipes or opaque parameters.

sports.previewSource.description: Preview and safely verify one public unauthenticated sports publisher and optional followed targets before confirmation. Returned headline samples are external publisher content.

sports.previewSourceAssignments.description: Preview an exact replacement assignment set for one sports source. Added target samples are external publisher content.

sports.rebuildSourceRecipe.description: Preview a bounded safe rebuild of one saved sports source recipe without changing it. Samples are external publisher content.

sports.confirmSource.description: Confirm a sports source from its actor-bound preview using the exact displayed publisher, hosts, targets, and authorization acknowledgement.

sports.confirmSourceAssignments.description: Confirm the exact actor-bound sports source assignment replacement shown by the preview.

sports.confirmSourceRecipe.description: Confirm the exact actor-bound sports source recipe rebuild shown by the preview.

sports.retrySource.description: Retry every verified target for one actor-owned sports source through pinned safe fetch with no browser.

sports.removeSource.description: Remove one actor-owned sports source and its assignments.

sports.followedFactsToday.description: Today's facts for the actor's followed teams and leagues, in the actor's time zone, with a bounded evidence block. Reads only the actor's own follows and public scoreboards. Never fails; a source that cannot be read gives a degraded, empty answer.

sports.heartbeatNextFixtures.description: The actor's next followed fixtures from the cached scoreboards only, with a revision, the next boundary and a freshness label. Never calls the sports provider.

sports.latestResult.description: The most recent result for a named team or a followed team, using the same rules as the Sports latest-result route.

sports.followTeam.description: Follow a league, or one team in a league, for the active actor. Checked against the provider's team list.

sports.unfollowTeam.description: Stop following a league or team for the active actor. Does nothing if it is not followed.
